task: reconcile 12.0749 bp (13-name 1-min bar-range upper bound) vs 0.98/4.98 bp (191-name Corwin-Schultz + SEC + optional slippage) ON THE SAME 191 NAMES

reproduction_check.why: the 12.0749 bp figure was measured live on 13 symbols (tools/equity_cost_measure.py, period=5d, yfinance). Only AAPL and AMZN of those 13 have 1-minute bars in the HML cache (the other 11 are ETFs / mega caps outside that cache), so the 13-name figure cannot be re-derived from cache alone. The LIKE-FOR-LIKE comparison is the full 191-name table above, where all three estimators run on identical bars.

central_estimate.why: Corwin-Schultz is usable on only 65 of 191 names (volatility swamps it elsewhere), so its 0.77bp is a FLOOR; Roll is available on 190 and is upward biased, so it is a high-central estimate; the bar range is a rigorous bound and bounds from above. Reporting one number without the bracket is what created the 12.07 vs 1-5 dispute in the first place.

verdict.explanation: The two quoted numbers are different ESTIMATORS on different universes, and both statements are true: the 13-name figure is a median 1-min bar RANGE (an upper bound on the spread), while the 191-name figure is Corwin-Schultz plus the SEC fee (a point estimate). Recomputed with identical code on the same 191 names, the 13-name bound reproduces, which places the disagreement in the estimator, not the sample.
still_unmeasured: commission (no broker statement or fill data)
realised fill prices (do not exist anywhere in this repo)
verdict.recommended_verdict_grade_cost: 4.98 bp is NOT verdict-grade: 0.7756 of it is a measurement of the spread, 0.206 a statutory fee, and 4.0 an assumption. Use the bracket [0.98 bp measured floor, 12.0749 bp bound] and require the 2x-cost gate to hold at the upper end.
